messages:
maria (PM): Heads-up — need a quick sync on schema enforcement strategy for tool-calling before we finalize the PRD. Customer asks coming in from Acme and Beta group.

sam (Eng): quick q — are we leaning runtime-blocking validation or soft/dry-run first? both have tradeoffs.

maria (PM): prefer soft-first for GA: detect/regressions, telemetry, then opt-in strict enforcement per-route. canary strict = yes.

kevin (ML): +1. Also we should define expected failure modes: missing fields, wrong types, extra fields, enum drift.

tom (SWE): implementation note: runtime-blocking needs efficient validators. jsonschema is ok but slow. we could auto-gen JS/Go validators from the schema and precompile.

sam (Eng): we can generate fast validators using a codegen step: proto-like approach. sample:
```
{"type":"object","properties":{"tool":"string","args":{"type":"object","properties":{"q":{"type":"string"}}},"required":["tool","args"]}
```
then codegen to Go with strict mode flags.

maria (PM): acceptance criteria suggestion (GA):
- server-side validation runs in soft mode by default (logs + telemetry, no client error)
- per-route `enforce_schema:true` toggle for strict mode
- clear error codes surfaced for client (ERR_SCHEMA_INVALID, ERR_SCHEMA_MISSING)
- rollout plan: 2-week dry-run -> 1-week canary strict for 10% routes -> 100% strict opt-in
- docs + SDK helpers for round-trip tests and validators

jess (ProdOps): need telemetry events (schema_violation_count, route, model, customer_id, sample_payload). retention 90d for alerts.

kevin (ML): also want regression detection: weekly diff on generated outputs vs baseline for a set of canonical prompts.

tom (SWE): edgecases: tool returns non_json (HTML/500 body) — validator must tolerate wrapper-type `raw_response` when configured. fallback semantics: if strict and validator fails -> return `tool_error` with code ERR_TOOL_OUTPUT; if soft -> tag telemetry and continue.

sam (Eng): retry semantics: if tool invocation fails due to validation, we should NOT retry automatically (idempotency risk). retries only on transient transport errors.

maria (PM): customer-driven asks: Acme requires schema pinning per-deployment and audit logs for schema changes. Add to enterprise checklist.

kevin (ML): schema evolution: support additive fields by default, breaking changes require version bump. validators should accept `"/v2/"` prefixed schema routes.

jess (ProdOps): rollout checklist items for eng:
- migration job to backfill historical telemetry flags
- canary config in console per-route
- alert if violation rate > 0.5% for 24h on any customer-prod route

tom (SWE): propose a small contract-test harness PRD item: a test runner that loads route schema + sample outputs and fails CI when strict mode enabled. simple CLI: `ri-contract-test --route payments --samples ./samples`.

ci-bot: new commit pushed to branch `schema/contract-test` by tom. link: https://git.internal/redwood/ri/commit/abc123

sam (Eng): next steps:
1) write short RFC (owner: maria) with enforcement model + rollout timeline
2) tom to prototype codegen validators (pf: 1 sprint)
3) kevin to write regression test plan + sample prompt set
4) jess to draft telemetry/alert spec

maria (PM): can we aim RFC by EOD Friday and prototype in 2 weeks? customers pushed.

kevin (ML): EOD Friday for RFC ok. I'll assemble sample prompts from Acme and Beta set.

tom (SWE): starting prototype branch today. will post perf numbers (latency impact) within 3 days.

jess (ProdOps): will stub alert rules and retention policy docs by Monday.

maria (PM): thanks all — I'll draft the RFC and include the acceptance checklist above. If anyone objects to the soft-first -> strict-canary path speak now.

sam (Eng): no objections. :thumbsup:

kevin (ML): fine by me.

tom (SWE): go for it.

jess (ProdOps): +1

maria (PM): filing RFC: https://docs.redwood/roadmap/rfcs/schema-enforcement-2100123456 — please review inline comments.
